prompt:
You help a busy software engineer (job hunting, runs small open-source game projects) PRIORITISE his inbox. Do not decide what to do with an item; only estimate its priority on two scales:
- urgency 0-100: how soon he must look at it (100 = right now, 0 = can wait weeks)
- importance 0-100: how much it matters to him (100 = career/project critical, 0 = noise)
Your own prioritising rubric from last round:
* Prioritize based on the urgency and importance of the task, not the sender's role.
* Consider the impact of the task on the software engineer's career and project, not just the sender's role.
* Evaluate the time sensitivity of the task, not just the sender's role.
Also write a summary badge of at most 6 words that would help him prioritise it at a glance.
Items (id | sender | subject | snippet):
p011 | Application update · Talentloop | Your application was viewed | A recruiter at a logistics scale-up viewed your application for 'ML engineer'.
p027 | Team · Promptly AI | Meet your new AI co-pilot for email | Sign up today and get 3 months free. Cancel anytime.
p028 | Code host notifications | [games] PR #14 review requested | 'Add hold piece to Tetris' – 6 files changed, +212 −40. You are a requested reviewer.
p014 | Webinar team · DataHarbor | Last chance to register: AI in logistics | Join 2,000 leaders on Thursday. Seats are filling up fast.
r002-llama323b-04 | Marketing · TechHub | New Product Launch: Get Ready for the Future | Our new product is launching soon.
urgency and importance must be whole numbers 0-100. Example of the format for one item: {"id":"x01","urgency":30,"importance":70,"summary":"Interview prep notes, this week"}
Return JSON only: {"items":[ one object per item above, 5 objects, same ids ]}
